message.content:
{"decision": "APPLY", "workflow_yaml": "name: Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [master, dev]
  pull_request:
    branches: [master, dev]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    name: Core and UI tests (iOS 27)
    runs-on: xcode-27
    timeout-minutes: 35
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1
        with:
          xcode-version: '27.0'
      - name: Boot available iOS 27 simulator
        run: |
          device_id=$(python3 .github/scripts/select-simulator.py)
          xcrun simctl bootstatus "$device_id" -b
          echo "IOS_SIMULATOR_ID=$device_id" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          mkdir -p artifacts
      - name: Core and real-engine tests
        working-directory: Packages/SwiftRadioCore
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          xcodebuild test -scheme SwiftRadioCore \
            -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$IOS_SIMULATOR_ID" \
            -derivedDataPath "$RUNNER_TEMP/SwiftRadioCore" \
            -resultBundlePath "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/artifacts/Core.xcresult" \
            -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile \
            -parallel-testing-enabled NO -collect-test-diagnostics never \
            -test-timeouts-enabled YES -maximum-test-execution-time-allowance 180 \
            -jobs 2 CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO 2>&1 | tee "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/artifacts/core.log"
      - name: UI regression tests
        # Live radio availability is a separate integration check. All
        # remaining UI tests run; failures are retained rather than retried away.
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          xcodebuild test -project SwiftRadio.xcodeproj -scheme SwiftRadio \
            -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$IOS_SIMULATOR_ID" \
            -derivedDataPath "$RUNNER_TEMP/SwiftRadioUI" \
            -resultBundlePath "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/artifacts/UI.xcresult" \
            -skip-testing:SwiftRadioUITests/SwiftRadioUITests/testPopupNavigationAndRefresh \
            -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile \
            -parallel-testing-enabled NO -collect-test-diagnostics never \
            -test-timeouts-enabled YES -default-test-execution-time-allowance 120 \
            -maximum-test-execution-time-allowance 180 \
            -jobs 2 CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO 2>&1 | tee artifacts/ui.log
      - name: Retain test results and screenshots
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: test-results-ios27
          path: artifacts/
          retention-days: 14", "rationale": "The workflow runs the same test job on every push and pull request to master/dev. When multiple commits land on the same branch in quick succession, older in-progress runs become superseded by newer ones. Adding a concurrency group scoped by workflow and ref with cancel-in-progress cancels those superseded runs while letting the latest run complete fully, preserving all build and test coverage. This matches P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: runs represent the same workflow and branch/PR, a newer revision supersedes older checks, the work is testing (not release/deployment), and distinct branches are isolated by the ref-scoped group. No new permissions, secrets, or network access are introduced.", "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]}

The user wants me to propose a CI optimization for the given workflow based on evidence. Let me analyze the workflow and the available evidence.

The workflow:
- Name: Tests
- Triggers: push to master/dev, pull_request to master/dev
- Single job: "test" running on xcode-27, timeout 35 minutes
- Steps: checkout, setup-xcode, boot simulator, core tests, UI regression tests, upload artifacts

Available evidence patterns:
1. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE - Cache dependency downloads
2. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST - Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure
3. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE - Cancel superseded runs
4. P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW - Skip explicitly dispensable workflow runs
5. P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER - Filter workflow triggers by changed paths
6. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT - Bound jobs with a custom timeout
7. P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE - Pause repeatedly failing scheduled workflows
8. P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE - Suppress schedules during repository inactivity
9. P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST - Run previously failing jobs first
10. P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT - Derive timeout candidates from successful history
11. P-LIT-PRIORITIZE - Prioritize tests for early failure feedback
12. P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY - Prioritize queued builds
13. P-LIT-SELECT - Select tests using change dependencies
14. P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT - Select builds using change or outcome predictions
15. P-LIT-BAZEL-PARALLEL - Tune Bazel build parallelism
16. P-LIT-BAZEL-INCREMENTAL - Cache Bazel build results
17. P-LIT-BAZEL-DEPS - Evaluate dependency cache overhead
18. P-LIT-ENV-CACHE - Reuse validated build environments
19. P-LIT-UNAFFECTED-STEPS - Skip steps using traced dependencies
20. P-LIT-SMELL-REPAIR - Repair evidenced configuration smells
21. P-LIT-DURATION-PREDICTION - Predict duration to guide investigation
22. P-LIT-UNUSED-OUTPUTS - Remove genuinely unused outputs
23. P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE - Share cached build dependencies
24. P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE - Reuse work across compatible configurations
25. P-LIT-UNUSED-DEP-SKIP - Evaluate skipping unused-dependency updates

Also experiment examples:
- P-LIT-FAIL-FAST (synthetic, scenario_passed)
- P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (measured_ci_workflow_on_fork, 26.8% savings)
- P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE (synthetic)
- P-LIT-DURATION-PREDICTION (synthetic)

Let me think about what fits this workflow:

1. The workflow has a single job, no matrix. So P-LIT-FAIL-FAST doesn't apply (no matrix).
2. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: The job already has timeout-minutes: 35. Could we reduce it? But we don't have history data showing successful runs are much faster. The CI history shows runs but no durations. Actually, the runs show created_at and updated_at, so we could compute durations:
   - Run 37350931054: 17:46:26 to 17:59:18 = ~12.9 min
   - Run 37347483851: 17:18:50 to 17:37:24 = ~18.6 min (failure)
   - Run 37344726530: 16:56:59 to 17:20:01 = ~23 min (failure)
   
   But these are historical_context_only, not measured baseline. The pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT requires "Representative successful-duration history exists". We have one successful run at ~12.9 min. The current timeout is 35 min. But reducing timeout is risky without more data. The experiment example for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT showed 26.8% savings by setting timeout-minutes: 5 on a workflow that presumably had no timeout or higher. But that was a different workflow (Checks with Node.js).

3. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: Cancel superseded runs. This applies when runs represent the same workflow and branch/PR and a newer revision supersedes older checks. This workflow runs on push and pull_request to master/dev. This could apply - if multiple pushes happen to the same branch, older runs could be cancelled. This is a GitHub Actions feature (concurrency). This preserves coverage since it only cancels superseded runs of the same workflow/branch.

4. P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER: Filter by changed paths. But the workflow tests iOS code, and changes could affect things broadly. Contraindication: "Shared configuration, generators or dependencies affect supposedly unrelated paths". This is risky for an Xcode project where many files are interconnected.

5. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: Cache dependency downloads. This is an Xcode/Swift project. Dependencies are Swift packages resolved from resolved file. The workflow uses `-onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile`. There's no explicit dependency caching step. `actions/checkout@v4` is used. For Swift projects, dependency caching could be done via `actions/cache` for `.build` directory or `~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm`. But this requires careful implementation. The evidence says "Repeated dependency fetching is measurable" and "Cache inputs include lockfile and environment". For Swift, the Package.resolved is the lockfile. This could be applicable.

6. P-LIT-ENV-CACHE: Reuse validated build environments. Requires pinned dependencies and resettable state. Xcode/Swift could benefit but complex.

Let me think about the best fit:

P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE seems like a good fit. The workflow runs on every push to master/dev. If a developer pushes multiple commits in quick succession, older runs become superseded. Adding concurrency with cancel-in-progress would save CI resources without reducing test coverage - it only cancels runs that are superseded by newer ones on the same branch.

The evidence for P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE:
- pattern_id: P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE
- document_id: pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE
- Evidence scope: literature_report_and_analyst_example
- Reported result: "Superseding runs can reduce duplicate work." metrics: vm_time_reduction_percent free: 1.9, paid: 4.1
- Preconditions: "Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR", "A newer revision supersedes older checks"
- Contraindications: "Release or deployment work", "Distinct branches share a cancellation group"

This workflow is not release/deployment work. It's tests on master/dev. Distinct branches don't share cancellation groups by default in GitHub Actions concurrency (you can scope by branch). So this seems applicable.

The implementation would be adding a `concurrency` key to the workflow:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

This cancels in-progress runs when a new run starts on the same branch/ref. This preserves test coverage because the latest run still completes fully.

Wait, but I need to check: does this weaken permissions or add privileged actions? No, concurrency is a native GitHub Actions feature, no new permissions needed.

Let me also consider P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT. The job has timeout-minutes: 35. The successful run took ~13 minutes. But we only have one successful run in history, and the evidence says "Representative successful-duration history exists" as a precondition. With only one data point, this is weak. Also, reducing timeout could cause valid slow runs to fail. The contraindication is "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit". Xcode tests can be variable. I think this is riskier.

P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: For Swift Package Manager, we could add caching of `.build` directory. But the workflow uses `xcodebuild test` which builds derived data to `$RUNNER_TEMP`. The SPM dependencies would be in the package directory. Caching could help but adds complexity and the evidence is observational with modest benefit. Also, the pattern says "Choose dependency download state rather than unchecked build outputs" and "Keep installation and all required tests". This could work but is more complex than concurrency.

I think P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is the cleanest, most supported optimization for this workflow. It's a minimal change, preserves all test coverage, and is directly supported by evidence.

Let me also check the experiment examples for P-LIT-FAIL-FAST - but there's no matrix in this workflow, so it doesn't apply.

Let me go with P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE.

The updated workflow would add:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

This should be placed at the top level, after permissions or before jobs.

    branches: [master, dev]

          xcrun simctl bootstatus "$device_id" -b
          echo "IOS_SIMULATOR_ID=$device_id" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          mkdir -p artifacts
      - name: Core and real-engine tests
        working-directory: Packages/SwiftRadioCore
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          xcodebuild test -scheme SwiftRadioCore \
            -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$IOS_SIMULATOR_ID" \
            -derivedDataPath "$RUNNER_TEMP/SwiftRadioCore" \
            -resultBundlePath "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/artifacts/Core.xcresult" \
            -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile \
            -parallel-testing-enabled NO -collect-test-diagnostics never \
            -test-timeouts-enabled YES -maximum-test-execution-time-allowance 180 \
            -jobs 2 CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO 2>&1 | tee "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/artifacts/core.log"
      - name: UI regression tests
        # Live radio availability is a separate integration check. All
        # remaining UI tests run; failures are retained rather than retried away.
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          xcodebuild test -project SwiftRadio.xcodeproj -scheme SwiftRadio \
            -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$IOS_SIMULATOR_ID" \
            -derivedDataPath "$RUNNER_TEMP/SwiftRadioUI" \
            -resultBundlePath "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/artifacts/UI.xcresult" \
            -skip-testing:SwiftRadioUITests/SwiftRadioUITests/testPopupNavigationAndRefresh \
            -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile \
            -parallel-testing-enabled NO -collect-test-diagnostics never \
            -test-timeouts-enabled YES -default-test-execution-time-allowance 120 \
            -maximum-test-execution-time-allowance 180 \
            -jobs 2 CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO 2>&1 | tee artifacts/ui.log
      - name: Retain test results and screenshots
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:

          path: artifacts/
          retention-days: 14

No experiment example for P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE specifically, but the pattern itself is in the pattern_catalogue.

- "Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR" - Yes, this workflow runs on push/PR to master/dev. The concurrency group can be scoped by github.ref.
